Order 29/01/2025

By way of filing the present criminal revision petition under Section 397 read with 401 Cr.P.C., the accused-petitioner has challenged the judgment dated 15.10.1998 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sirohi whereby he has been convicted for the offence under section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the judgment dated 05.06.2006 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Sirohi in criminal appeal no. 44/2003 whereby the judgment of the trial court has been affirmed.

The learned trial court vide order dated 15.10.1998 has sentenced the accused petitioner No.1 to six months' S.I and a fine of Rs.1,000/- and in default of payment of fine to further undergo one and a half months' S.I.
As per prosecution, on 09.03.1993 the samples of chilli powder were taken from the petitioner No.1 who is proprietor of petitioner No.2 - firm.
The samples were sent for examination to the Public Analyst, Jodhpur after duly following the procedure provided under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
: RJ-JD:5801] (2 of 4) [CRLR-465/2006] Public Analyst in its report found the chilli powder samples to be 'Adulterated'.
On the basis of the report of the Public Analyst, the petitioner was prosecuted for the offence under section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
During the course of trial, the prosecution examined as many as 5 witnesses and 20 documents were exhibited.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents.
He further submitted that the incident in the present case occurred in the year 1993.

There is no positive evidence available on record regarding the adding of starch and artificial colour in the red chilli powder by the petitioner and in the absence thereof, only on the basis of the report of Public Analyst, it cannot be said that the petitioner had committed the alleged crime or the red chilli powder was adulterated.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the sentence awarded to the petitioner has alreadyu been suspended by this Court vide order dated 20.06.2006.

Learned counsel for the petitioner in the alternative submitted that since the occurrence relates to year 1993 and the petitioner has already served some part of the sentence awarded to him, therefore,
the substantive sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him.

Reliance was placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Puttaswamy v State of Karnataka:
2009 (1) WLC (SC) (Cri.) 623 and a judgment of Coordinate [2025:RJ-JD:5801] (3 of 4) [CRLR-465/2006] Bench of this Court in the case of Kamla Prasad v. State of Rajasthan: 2014 CriLJ 2582.
Per Contra learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the learned courts below have rightly awarded the sentence against the petitioner.

sentences.text: There is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgments/orders and therefore, the same do not call for any interference by this Court in exercise of revisional jurisdiction.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the record of the case.
This Court finds concurrent finding of fact with regard to petitioner being guilty of mixing maiz starch and sudan-04 red colour in the red chilli powder.

This Court finds that the petitioner is the proprietor of the petitioner No.2 - firm and therefore there is no reason available with it to disbelieve the report of the Public Analyst, wherein the samples drawn from the chilli powder were found to be 'Adulterated'.

However, in the opinion of this Court, since the incident relates to the year 1993 and the petitioner has suffered the agony and trauma of protracted trial for about 31 years coupled with the fact that the petitioner has spent some period in custody, it will be just and proper if the sentence awarded by the trial court for the offence under section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is reduced to the period already undergone by the petitioner.
In the result, the revision petition is partly allowed.

While maintaining the petitioner's conviction, his sentence for the offence under section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is hereby reduced to the period already undergone by him.
